title: Resolution of Vectors — Worked Examples
notes: **Q1. Two forces, 10 N acting at 30° above the +x-axis and 5 N acting at 45° below the +x-axis, act at a point. Find the resultant.** $F_x = 10\cos30° + 5\cos45° = 8.66+3.54=12.20\,\text{N}$. $F_y = 10\sin30° - 5\sin45° = 5-3.54=1.46\,\text{N}$ (the second force's y-component is negative since it is below the axis). $F=\sqrt{F_x^2+F_y^2}=\sqrt{12.20^2+1.46^2}\approx12.28\,\text{N}$, at $\theta=\tan^{-1}(1.46/12.20)\approx6.8°$ above the x-axis.

**Q2. Two forces, 10 N and 5 N, each act at 30° from a common reference line, one above it and one below it. Find the resultant.** $F_x = 10\cos30°+5\cos30° = (10+5)\times(\sqrt3/2)=7.5\sqrt3\approx12.99\,\text{N}$. $F_y = 10\sin30° - 5\sin30° = 5-2.5=2.5\,\text{N}$. $F=\sqrt{F_x^2+F_y^2}=\sqrt{12.99^2+2.5^2}\approx13.23\,\text{N}$, at $\theta=\tan^{-1}(2.5/12.99)\approx10.9°$ from the reference line, on the side of the larger (10 N) force.
Each force is replaced by F cosθ along x and F sinθ along y, with θ measured from the positive x-axis. A force below the axis has a negative sine.
For 10 N at 30° above the axis and 5 N at 45° below it, F_x = 10 cos30° + 5 cos45° and F_y = 10 sin30° − 5 sin45°.
The resultant is sqrt(12.2^2 + 1.46^2) = 12.3 N, a little above the +x-axis because F_y is positive and small.
confusion: A force below the axis still has a positive x-component if it points to the right.
Do not add 10 N and 5 N directly.
sin and cos are fixed once θ is measured from the x-axis.
The resultant is not the larger component.

summary: Resolve every force from the same axis, keep the sign of a component that points downward, add the columns, and only then take Pythagoras. The small positive F_y in the 10 N and 5 N example puts the resultant just above the x-axis.
